ceiling_proof_reverse_leg.conclusion: 6 of 8 chloride-environment classes have EXACTLY ZERO marine-calibration rows in the reverse leg. Any Mondrian-by-chloride-class calibrator (at any MIN_CLASS_N threshold, any granularity) can only ever assign a stratum-specific quantile to test rows in the 'halide' or 'other' classes (the only two with nonzero marine-cal mass); all other test rows are PROVABLY forced to the pooled/marginal quantile by construction, not by a tunable hyperparameter. Lowering MIN_CLASS_N from 5 towards 1 (tested: no change, zero-count classes are zero at any threshold) cannot reach these rows. This mechanism has a hard, provable ceiling, not merely an empirically-observed one.
